purpose: Primary-source bounds for exact-owned async deletion/recreation calibration; these are documentation statements, not native observations.

quotes: If the function returns an error, by default Lambda attempts to run it two more times, with a one-minute wait between the first two attempts, and two minutes between the second and third attempts.
For throttling errors (429) and system errors (500-series), Lambda returns the event to the queue and attempts to run the function again for up to 6 hours by default.
The retry interval increases exponentially from 1 second after the first attempt to a maximum of 5 minutes.
Even if your function doesn't return an error, it's possible for it to receive the same event from Lambda multiple times because the queue itself is eventually consistent.
sources.boundary: This text names 429 and 500-series errors, not deleted-target404; it does not establish404 terminal scheduling or reincarnation behavior.

quotes: By default, Lambda retries an asynchronous invocation twice if the function returns an error. It retains events in a queue for up to six hours.
The maximum age of a request that Lambda sends to a function for processing.
The maximum number of times to retry when the function returns an error.
sources.boundary: API configuration readback is not a demonstrated queue application barrier. This probe requires completed same-target retry and age controls before deletion.

quotes: When you set reserved concurrency to zero for an asynchronously invoked function, Lambda begins sending new events to the configured dead-letter queue or the on-failure event destination, without any retries.
To prevent a function from triggering, you can set the function's reserved concurrency to zero.

Each function can have multiple destinations, so you can configure separate destinations for successful and failed events. Like error handling settings, you can configure destinations on a function, function version, or alias.
sources.permission: SQS destinations require sqs:SendMessage on the execution role.
sources.boundary: Reserved concurrency zero is not used as a queuing barrier; a real synchronous blocker occupies the single reserved slot, and a synchronous429 is required.

sources.quote: A Lambda alias is a pointer to a function version that you can update.
sources.boundary: This establishes mutable alias routing, not whether already queued events resolve it again.

sources.quote: To delete a specific function version, use the Qualifier parameter. Otherwise, all versions and aliases are deleted.
sources.boundary: The API page does not specify the fate of already accepted asynchronous events, nor same-name recreation semantics.
The API page does not specify terminal delivery, retained controls, or queued-event behavior after recreation.

quotes: Invocations aren't recorded if the invocation request is throttled or otherwise results in an invocation error.
Throttled requests and other invocation errors don't count as either Invocations or Errors.
If you configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) or OnFailure destination, then events are sent there before they're dropped.
sources.boundary: The last quote describes AsyncEventsDropped. Missing metric datapoints are not measured zero; this capture uses actual runtime messages and destination records rather than inferring terminal state from missing metrics.

sources.quote: Lambda assigns monotonically increasing sequence numbers for versioning. Lambda never reuses version numbers, even after you delete and recreate a function.
sources.boundary: Publication-number monotonicity is documented; it does not imply that accepted asynchronous events are fenced against same-name recreation.
